matched.actualTitle: XXE (XML External Entity) Injection - File Disclosure and SSRF
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify the same vulnerability in DOCX file processing. The actual finding confirms XXE exploitation through document-parser service with XXE_resolved=true responses and entity_content exfiltration. The vulnerability allows reading arbitrary files and SSRF attacks via DOCTYPE SYSTEM entity declarations, matching the expected finding's description of XXE in document processing with file:// and http:// URI resolution.

matched.actualTitle: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in M3U8 HLS Playlist Processing
matched.matchReason: Both findings describe identical SSRF vulnerability in M3U8/HLS playlist processing. The actual finding confirms that the video processor fetches URLs from M3U8 playlists without validation, enabling SSRF attacks against internal services. The actual finding explicitly documents SSRF exploitation with internal service discovery (image-processor:3001, video-processor:3002, document-parser:3003), directly matching the expected finding's scenario of uploading M3U8 files to access internal services.

missed.title: ImageTragick SVG Delegate Injection
missed.reason: The expected finding describes SVG delegate injection via ephemeral:| syntax in xlink:href attributes that should trigger simulate_command() execution. While the actual findings document extensive SSRF and XXE vulnerabilities, there is no evidence in the actual test results of SVG-specific ImageTragick exploitation, SVG processing vulnerabilities, or ephemeral:| command injection patterns being tested or discovered. This critical RCE vulnerability was not identified during the penetration test.

missed.title: MinIO Admin API Broken Access Control
missed.reason: The expected finding describes broken access control on MinIO admin API endpoints (/minio/admin/v3/info) where admin credentials obtained via XXE can be used to access restricted storage buckets. While the actual test found XXE vulnerabilities, there is no evidence of testing or discovering the MinIO admin API's broken access control, the /minio/admin/v3/info endpoint, or admin credential usage scenarios. This vulnerability linking XXE to storage access was not identified.

missed.title: Information Exposure via Unrestricted Flag Access
missed.reason: The expected finding describes a flag stored in internal-secrets bucket at /internal-secrets/flag.txt accessible with admin credentials through a 5-step exploitation chain. While the actual findings document information disclosure and XXE vulnerabilities, there is no evidence of attempting to retrieve flags, testing admin-only bucket access controls, or confirming the internal-secrets bucket existence. This final stage of the expected vulnerability chain was not identified in actual testing.

extra.title: Information Disclosure - Version and Internal Service URLs Exposed via API Endpoints
extra.assessment: NEW DISCOVERY - Valid security finding. The application exposes software version (2.0.0), internal service URLs (image-processor:3001, video-processor:3002, document-parser:3003), backend architecture, and engine information without authentication. This enables reconnaissance for targeted attacks and is not in the expected findings list but represents legitimate security weakness.

extra.title: Stack Trace Information Disclosure via Error Messages
extra.assessment: NEW DISCOVERY - Valid security finding. Multiple endpoints return detailed Node.js stack traces with file paths, library names, and internal structure when given malformed JSON. This is a systemic vulnerability affecting entire application error handling. Not in expected findings but represents significant information disclosure.

extra.title: Complete API Documentation Exposed Without Authentication
extra.assessment: NEW DISCOVERY - Valid security finding. Root endpoint returns complete API documentation including all endpoints, supported formats, and internal architecture without authentication. While related to information disclosure findings, this specific comprehensive documentation exposure was not in the expected findings list.

extra.title: SSRF - Unvalidated URL Parameter Acceptance in /api/upload
extra.assessment: NEW DISCOVERY - Valid security finding. The /api/upload endpoint accepts unvalidated SSRF-like parameters (url, uri, fetch, target, source, callback) without validation. While the test environment doesn't make actual outbound requests, this represents a real SSRF vulnerability vector not in the expected findings.

extra.title: Path Traversal in File Upload Endpoint
extra.assessment: NEW DISCOVERY - Valid security finding. The /api/upload/raw endpoint accepts path traversal sequences (../) in the filename query parameter without validation or normalization. Payloads like ../../../etc/passwd.pdf are accepted with HTTP 200, allowing potential file write outside intended directory. This is a critical vulnerability not in the expected findings list.

extra.title: Information Disclosure: Service Configuration and Engine Details via /api/status
extra.assessment: NEW DISCOVERY - Valid security finding. The /api/status endpoint exposes internal service engines (imagemagick-sim, ffmpeg-sim, docparser-sim, minio-sim), configuration details, and bucket counts without authentication. Enables targeted attacks on identified technologies. Not in expected findings but legitimate security weakness.

extra.title: Application-Wide Stack Trace Information Disclosure
extra.assessment: NEW DISCOVERY - Valid security finding. Comprehensive documentation that all POST endpoints (/, /api/formats, /api/upload, /api/upload/raw, /api/status, /health) return detailed stack traces when given malformed JSON. This systemic error handling issue affects entire application. Not in expected findings but represents critical information disclosure vulnerability.

extra.title: Potential Deserialization Vulnerability in Upload Endpoint - Unconfirmed
extra.assessment: FALSE POSITIVE / UNCONFIRMED - The actual finding documents that comprehensive testing did not confirm a triggerable deserialization vulnerability. All test payloads (serialization objects, polyglots, malformed files) were processed without execution. This is documented as unconfirmed and should not be considered a valid finding. Included in actual results but lacks definitive proof of exploitability.
